subject: Anthropology
title: Caste and Social Hierarchy
description: A micro-lesson that makes Caste and Social Hierarchy usable.

hook.text: In India, a person's caste once decided their job, spouse, diet, and social circle from birth. No escape.

buildup.text: Caste is a rigid social hierarchy where rank is inherited at birth and determines life chances and social contact.

discovery.text: Louis Dumont argued that Indian caste is based on purity and pollution — the pure must not contact the impure.

twist.text: Caste-like systems exist beyond India. Japan's Burakumin and racism in America share structural similarities.

climax.text: Caste reveals that inequality can be cultural bedrock — so deeply embedded it feels natural and inevitable.

punchline.text: The deepest hierarchies feel like nature.

quiz.question: What distinguishes caste from other hierarchies?
options: Rank is inherited at birth and rarely changeable

details.summary: Caste systems are rigid hereditary social hierarchies where status is determined at birth and cannot be changed through individual effort. The Indian caste system is the most studied example, but caste-like structures appear in many societies worldwide.
details.whyItMatters: Caste demonstrates how social inequality can be naturalized through cultural and religious frameworks, making inherited privilege seem inevitable and divinely ordained rather than humanly constructed and potentially changeable.
takeaways: Caste is a rigid hereditary hierarchy determined at birth
It is maintained through cultural and religious justification
Caste-like structures appear in many societies beyond India

faq.question: How does caste differ from class?
faq.answer: Class is theoretically open — individuals can move between classes through economic mobility. Caste is closed — membership is determined at birth and cannot be changed. In practice, class systems also restrict mobility, but caste makes immobility explicit and ideologically justified.

faq.question: Does caste still affect people in modern India?
faq.answer: Despite legal abolition of caste discrimination, caste profoundly affects marriage, employment, education, and social interaction in India today. Dalits and lower-caste groups continue to face systematic disadvantage and discrimination despite decades of affirmative action policies.
